[Learn more about visiting in the fall and winter seasons.](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/on/bruce/activ/hiver-winter) **Closure Alert** The Visitor Centre and parking lot will be closed **November 12-13 and November 16-18, 2026**, for siding work. Dates may be extended if required. The Visitor Centre and parking lot will remain open November 14-15, 2026. - **Burnt Point Loop Access: During the closure, visitors may** park in town and access the Burnt Point Loop via the Bruce Trail. A signed detour will be in place behind the Visitor Centre. **Trail Closure: November 1 to 23, 2026** Sections of the Bruce Trail between Crane Lake and Halfway Log Dump, and between Marr Lake and Little Cove (including Driftwood Cove), will be closed for Saugeen Ojibway Nation hunting activities. Please obey all closure signage and avoid closed areas. More information: [Important Bulletin](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/on/bruce/securite-safety/bulletins) In the traditional territory of the Saugeen Ojibway Nation, this scenic park features towering cliffs of the Niagara Escarpment plunging into the blue waters of Georgian Bay. World famous hiking in a rugged landscape, home to orchids, ferns and black bears. # Fall and winter camping

## Bruce Peninsula National Park

### Reservations for winter camping and yurts open on Tuesday, November 17, 2026

The winter camping season runs from December 15, 2026, to April 30, 2027

Reservations for front country camping at the Tamarack section of Cyprus Lake Campground and backcountry campsites at Stormhaven campground can be [booked online](https://reservation.pc.gc.ca/).

Please note: Winter camping is walk-in tent camping only. Car, van, trailer and RV camping is not available during the winter months.

### December 15 to April 30

The Bruce Peninsula is spectacular in all seasons. Fall and winter camping is a great way to experience the natural beauty of the area. There are a few things you should know before you arrive.

#### Online       [External link:  Reservation Service](https://reservation.pc.gc.ca/)

#### By phone       [Phone: 1-877-737-3783](tel:18777373783)    [Phone: 1-519-826-5391 outside North America](tel:15198265391)

#### The basics

Expect limited service in the winter, both in the park and in the surrounding area. The Parks Canada Visitor Centre and Cyprus Lake Campground Office will be open over the winter ( [see hours of operation](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/on/bruce/visit/heures-hours)). There is a gas station, grocery store, post office, liquor store, and a handful of other businesses that stay open throughout the year in the town of Tobermory. Hours are limited. Check [www.tobermory.com](http://www.tobermory.com/ "Tobermory Tourism") for more information.

![snow covered picnic table](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/on/bruce/WET4/activ/neige_snow.jpg)

#### Winter Safety

- Winter conditions can be dangerous - be prepared and cautious
- Emergency response is limited during winter
- Cell phone reception is not reliable
- Make a trip plan and share it with someone
- Winter activity is more strenuous and daylight hours are short. Watch your time
- Be alert for exhaustion and hypothermia
- The shoreline becomes icy, especially at the Grotto/Indian Head Cove and the ice is often covered by snow - **Do not approach the edge**
- Danger of thin, moving ice on Georgian Bay. Do not walk on the ice!

Where can I camp?

**Yurt camping:**

- [Yurt camping](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/on/bruce/activ/camping/yurt) is available for the fall and winter season. A [reservation](https://reservation.pc.gc.ca/) with a two-night minimum is required
- Check-in at the Cyprus Lake Office
- Each yurt is equipped with a bunk bed (double bed below and single bed up top) and a double sized murphy bed
- A barbeque and a bear-proof bin to store scented items are provided. Cooking or storing food inside the yurt is not permitted
- The only heat source inside the yurt is a woodstove. Wood is available at the Cyprus Lake Campground Office or from local vendors in the Bruce Peninsula
- Cars are not permitted to park at the yurts. Sleds are available to bring belongings from the nearby parking lot.
- Candles or other open flames are not permitted
- Washroom facilities are located in the parking area, For sanitary purposes, please use the washrooms and not the surrounding forested areas.

**Front country camping:**

- Front country camping reservations are now available online! Visit the [reservation page](https://reservation.pc.gc.ca/) to book your site today
- Campsites are not directly accessible by vehicle. Parking is available nearby at the P2 parking lot and campers must walk with their gear to their campsite
- RV, trailer, van or car camping is not permitted during the winter months
- Services are limited, outhouse facilities are available in the campground
- Winter storms can impact road conditions. It is recommended to bring all required food and water supplies, including extra supplies in case of extreme weather
- Fires are permitted in designated fire pits only
- Burn locally sourced firewood which is available at the Cyprus Lake Office or from vendors in the Bruce Peninsula
- [Camping fees](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/on/bruce/visit/tarifs-fees) apply

**Backcountry camping (remote, hike in wilderness sites):**

- Book backcountry camping reservations online! Visit the [reservation page to book](https://reservation.pc.gc.ca/) your site today
- Please note hot tents are **not permitted** in the backcountry
- Fires and open flames are prohibited at all backcountry sites. If you see a fire, please alert park staff or call 1-877-852-3100
- Stormhaven backcountry sites ( [map](https://pcweb2.azureedge.net/-/media/pn-np/on/bruce/WET4/Maps-2025/BPFF_Backcountry_EN-2400.jpg))
  - Be prepared for a 3-4 hour hike from P2 parking lot
  - During the winter months, the cut-off time to access the trails to stormhaven is 3 hours before sunset

How do I register?

- Yurt camping requires a [reservation](https://reservation.pc.gc.ca/) and you must check-in at the Cyprus Lake office upon arrival to collect your permits
- Front and backcountry camping is available by [reservation](https://reservation.pc.gc.ca/)
- Front and backcountry campers must register at the Cyprus Lake office the day of arrival
  - Please keep in mind the cut-off time to access the trails for the backcountry is 3 hours before sunset for Stormhaven

How much does it cost?

Please visit our [fees page](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/on/bruce/visit/tarifs-fees) for more information.

- Yurts

  - Camping, reservation and daily admission fees apply
  - Extra vehicle parking fee applies if there is more than 1 vehicle per yurt

- Front country (Tamarack)

  - Camping and daily admission fees apply
  - Extra vehicle parking fee applies if there is more than 1 vehicle per campsite

- Backcountry camping (Stormhaven)
  - Camping, parking and daily admission fees apply

What should I bring?

##### Firewood

- The possession or use of firewood not supplied by Bruce Peninsula National Park or our verified sellers is prohibited
- Collecting firewood, sticks or twigs from the forest is prohibited

Everything you need to enjoy your camping. This includes:

- Tent or sleeping shelter. Campground is not plowed in winter months, tent camping only. RV, trailer, van or car camping not permitted.
- Warm sleeping bag and appropriate clothing.
- Food and water – there is no potable water in the winter. Grocery store hours are limited
- Cooking gear (stove, pots, pans, etc) and other standard camping gear.
- A hatchet for splitting firewood into kindling
- Anything you need to enjoy your experience.
- Don’t forget your lighter or waterproof matches.

Anything else I should know?

- Fires are only permitted in the designated fire pits at your yurt or at your campsite in the Tamaracks campground.
- Fires are not allowed anywhere else in the park, including the Stormhaven remote campsites.
- There is no running water available at front and backcountry campsites. Bring your own water or filtration system.
- Toilets are primitive at front and backcountry campsites. There are no flush toilets or running water. Please use the outhouse facilities for sanitary purposes, not the surrounding forest.
- Commercial businesses on the Bruce Peninsula are limited during the winter months.
- Make sure your vehicle is equipped for local road conditions (snow tires are recommended)
- You must pack out your garbage.
- Your cell phone may not work, in the campground, on the trails, or elsewhere in the park.

##### Winter conditions can be dangerous - be prepared and be cautious

Learn more about [winter safety](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/on/bruce/securite-safety/neige-snow) to ensure you are prepared for camping in the park.

# Camping and overnight accommodations

## Bruce Peninsula National Park

### Reservations for winter camping, winter backcountry camping at Stormhaven and yurts open on Tuesday, November 17, 2026

The winter camping season runs from December 15, 2026, to April 30, 2027

Bruce Peninsula National Park offers semi-wilderness, yurts and backcountry camping, in ideal locations for your park adventure.

**Campers staying at the Cyprus Lake Campground can hike to the Grotto from their campsite. If you’d like to park in the Grotto parking lot, you will need to [book a parking space](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/on/bruce/activ/emplacements-locations/parking) in the same manner as anyone else.**

Camping in the park is popular, **[reservations are required](https://reservation.pc.gc.ca/)** from May through October. Weekdays in the spring and fall offer opportunities with fewer people, natural attractions, bird migrations, spring flowers and fall colours.

Certain [**rules and regulations**](https://parks.canada.ca/pn-np/on/bruce/securite-safety/regle_regu) apply when camping at Bruce Peninsula National Park.

**Campground rules**

- The possession or use of firewood not supplied by Bruce Peninsula National Park or our verified sellers is prohibited
- Park staff will collect and destroy any firewood brought from outside the park to ensure Invasive Species are not introduced
- Do not collect wood or sticks off the ground
- Quiet hours are in effect from 10:00 pm to 7:00 am
- No excessive noise at anytime
- Alcohol and cannabis consumption bans are in effect during quiet hours
- Feeding campfires after 11 pm is prohibited
- Long weekends: A full ban on the possession of alcohol and cannabis are in effect. The weekends when alcohol and cannabis are not permitted in the park at any time are:
  - Victoria Day Long Weekend
  - Canada Day Long Weekend
  - Civic Holiday Long Weekend
  - Labour Day Long Weekend
  - Thanksgiving Long Weekend
- No visitors on site after 10:00 pm
- Sites are allowed a maximum of 6 people
- Sites are allowed a maximum of 3 sleeping structures
- Trailers & RVs must be emptied at the dumping station near Cyprus Lake Office
- Fireworks and drones are not permitted in national parks
- Portable toilets and shower units are not permitted
